newsitem.title: CHINA: France's Chirac sees bright future for China ties.
newsitem.headline: France's Chirac sees bright future for China ties.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac launched his first state visit to China on Thursday with a rallying cry to make China a major partner and a call for more French business with the world's fastest growing economy.
"China must be one of our main partners," he told the French Chamber of Commerce on the first day of a four-day visit.

"The China of tomorrow... will be one of the top nations of the world," he said. "I should like all my compatriots to share my conviction that despite the geographical distance between us, China must be one of our main partners."
Chirac echoed one of the favourite themes of Chinese President Jiang Zemin, who repeatedly calls for a multi-polar world in which no single country holds superpower status.
Chirac called for China to become a political partner of France -- "serving the cause of security and peace in the multi-polar world we want to organise together".
That goal would be the major theme of a joint communique to be signed by Chirac and Jiang later on Thursday and which will state their desire and determination to strengthen ties.

Chirac, accompanied by a huge delegation of French business leaders and expected to oversee the signing of hundreds of millions of dollars worth of business deals, seized the chance to promote more French trade and investment in China.

"For the first time in more than a century, China, which is no longer threatened on its borders, is enjoying exceptional stability and growth," he said, citing its considerable needs in infrastructure, energy and capital.

"France wishes to participate in this evolution. It is particarly well placed to do so," he said, adding that one year's worth of trade with China 25 years ago was equivalent to two weeks' trade today.

However, France was only China's 13th trading partner, he said. Chinese figures show exports to France reached $440 million last year while imports totalled $500 million with trade falling by 6.7 percent in 1996.
French exports declined by about 20 percent in the first quarter while imports rose 13 percent, Chinese figures showed.
However, France's Lafarge won approval from China on Thursday to increase its stake in a joint venture cement plant by an additional $75 million.

More deals were expected, with officials of Airbus Industrie rumoured to have wrangled with China into the early hours of Thursday to try to reach agreement on a potentially huge sale of airliners, French sources said.

France's Aerospatiale was expected to sign an agreement to sell airliners to China's Xinjiang Airlines, while a subsidiary was seen reaching a deal to produce helicopters in China. Other deals included a Rhone-Poulenc venture on insecticides for rice and a France Telecom venture on mobile telephones.
"We should also underline our great ambition for the aircraft industry," Chirac said, referring to a joint venture involving Airbus and China to produce a 100-seater plane.
China broke ground on Thursday on the Ling'ao nuclear power plant near Hong Kong for which French engineering group Framatome is supplying the main nuclear reactors.

Chirac said France backed China's bid to enter the World Trade Organisation, but said all members must adapt to the changing trends imposed by globalisation, fight against improper and unfair practices and ensure better protection of intellectual property rights -- all criticisms levelled at China.
